text: A FreeSWITCH channel that connects back over the outbound socket is handed to the endpoint whose X-Chappe-Call header it carries (variable_sip_h_X-Chappe-Call).
notes: connect_caller/3 and create_endpoint/1 get the channel of their own INVITE; the endpoint answers it

text: A channel whose X-Chappe-Call no endpoint waits for, or that carries none, is hung up.
notes: chappe behaviour: the socket gets execute hangup, then closes

text: The endpoint owner hears DTMF digits, the hangup with its cause, and the loss of the node the channel is on.
notes: {chappe_mrf, Ep, {dtmf, D} | {hangup, Cause} | {node_down, Node}}

text: When the endpoint owner exits, the audio forks and session recordings it started are stopped and the channel is killed.
notes: uuid_audio_fork stop, then uuid_kill; the caller gets a BYE

text: Moving a caller to an endpoint or a SIP target does not re-INVITE the caller; the leg it had gets a BYE.
notes: replace_b/3 behind rtpengine: no INVITE reaches the caller, the old channel or callee gets BYE

text: A bridge that fails leaves the caller where it was.
notes: bridge/2 to a direct call returns not_anchored and the endpoint keeps its dialog

text: A conference process owns its room: the room stays up when every member left, until the conference stops.
notes: native: the chappe_mix room outlives its first caller and the next caller joins the same room

text: Members join and leave with events to the conference receivers, and can be muted, made deaf, played to and kicked, on both backends.
notes: {chappe_mrf_conf, Conf, {joined | left | talking, Member, _}}; fs operations are conference <name> api commands

text: A locked conference refuses joins.
notes: join/3 returns {error, locked}

text: A member that has to enter a PIN joins only with the right one.
notes: fs backend: play_collect for the PIN, bad_pin after the tries; the call of a member bridged for the purpose is hung up

text: A REFER to a room is accepted only once the room's own checks (lease, target, admission) and its refer_policy allowed it; until then nothing is answered 200 and nothing is dialed.
notes: chappe behaviour: a refused REFER gets 403, 486, 503 or the policy's code, with no subscription and no dial

text: A party a REFER brings in becomes a member only once it answered: before that it is not listed, not in the roster, and nothing it sends reaches the room.
notes: native: the endpoint joins the mixer after CHANNEL_BRIDGE; fs: the member comes with add-member; the referrer hears 200 once it is in

text: A dial-out that fails (busy, declined, no answer, timeout) tells the referrer the status and leaves the room's members as they were.
notes: 486, 603, 480, 408 in the final NOTIFY; no joined or left event

text: A REFER that adds a party is admitted before anything is dialed, on both backends: a locked room refuses it 403, a full one 486, the parties being dialed counting as members.
notes: chappe_mrf_conf_backend:admission/1, shared with join/3

text: A REFER repeated from the same origin for the same target dials nobody again and hears the first one's outcome; adding a member already in answers 200 at once.
notes: chappe behaviour: ops keyed {origin, method, AOR}, done ones kept 32 s, at most 64 per room

text: A REFER with method=BYE removes the member whose endpoint entity the Refer-To is, else the one member with that address-of-record; more than one is 485, none 404, a referrer the policy refuses 403, and members of other rooms are never looked at.
notes: RFC 4579 5.11; the policy runs before the member is looked up, so a refused referrer learns nothing of the roster

text: The Replaces a Refer-To carries is put on the INVITE to the party, for a REFER in a member's dialog and outside any dialog.
notes: RFC 4579 5.10; the Referred-By goes on too, as a bare URI

text: A REFER with method=REFER makes the focus REFER the target to the conference URI, and the referrer's final status is the target's answer to that REFER.
notes: RFC 4579 5.7; the target's own NOTIFYs are kept with the op

text: The roster shows a party a REFER brought in as dialed-out and one that came with Referred-By as referred by that URI, each participant as a user by its address-of-record with one endpoint per member, and a member that leaves as disconnected (departed or booted) before it is deleted.
When a room ends, every REFER still under way gets a final NOTIFY 487 and its dial is given up.
notes: native: the dialing endpoint is destroyed; fs: uuid_kill of the dialed uuid

text: An out-of-dialog REFER whose Target-Dialog names a member's dialog with the room is from that member.
notes: RFC 4538 4: the policy sees member => Id; a Target-Dialog naming no dialog of the room is ignored
